newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euroshares suffer Wall Street double whammy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euroshares suffer Wall Street double whammy.

text.p: Europe's share markets were hammered on the first trading day of new year after Wall Street fell heavily on renewed inflation fears.
The U.S. blood-letting followed a 1.5 percent tumble in New York stocks on the last day of 1996.
"It's not a good start to the New Year," said one London share trader. "We're at the mercy of Wall Street and the U.S. is only as good as its last data."

London, Europe's busiest bourse, ended down 1.48 percent while French shares were off 2.54 percent and German shares closed floor trading down 1.38 percent, and were 2.06 percent lower in post-bourse electronic trading.

Wall Street's Dow Jones average of leading U.S. shares, having fallen 96 points earlier, was down more than 55 points, or 0.85 percent, shortly after European markets closed. It shed 101.10 points on Tuesday.

The Dow actually rose about 20 points at its open on Thursday on the back of a rise in the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits last week -- taken as a sign that the economy was not over-heating.
In its weekly jobless claims report, the U.S. Labour Department said new filings climbed to 366,000 in the week ended December 28, up from a revised 344,000 in the previous week.

But then another indicator, the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) report, showed that the U.S. economy was "real solid in December," raising fears that U.S. interest rates may to rise to counter the threat of inflation.
The NAPM index for December rose to 54.0, well above the forecast for 52.3. A figure above 50 indicates growth.
"It's the same old story -- the fear of rising interest rates," said one London share dealer earlier.
Higher rates spell bad news for share markets as returns on other investments and holding cash on deposit rise.
But Wall Street's latest falls barely dent its rise over the last two years, which has seen it gain over 60 percent, a run the likes of which has been seen only twice before, in 1927-28 and 1954-55.
The market's gains in 1996 came despite widespread predictions that inflation or weak corporate earnings would rain on Wall Street's parade.
European shares chased U.S. shares higher in 1996 when British stocks chalked up a gain of 11.6 percent, Frankfurt 28 percent and French shares almost 24 percent.
While the mood was more cautious on Thursday, many traders were still on holiday across Europe however and business was relatively thin, exaggerating share price movements.
London's FTSE 100 index of blue-chip shares lost 61.1 points to close at 4,057.4 after getting off to a poor start in the morning in response to sharp losses in the U.S. on Tuesday.
French and German shares also closed sharply down in thin volume, spooked by fears of higher U.S. interest rates following the NAPM data.
The dollar sank in late European trading after the NAPM data hit asset markets, ending around 1.5407 marks and 115.47 yen.

Although the stronger than expected NAPM survey points to a monetary tightening sooner rather than later the dollar is reacting more to what happens with capital flows than what happens with interest rates.

World oil prices began 1997 with a rally as freezing weather continued to grip much of Europe, stoking demand for winter heating oil and memories of a similar cold snap in the United States a year ago.
The February Brent crude oil futures contract on the International Petroleum Exchange was up 47 cents a barrel at $24.28 at around 1700 gmt, having been up 80 cents at one point.
Gold was fixed at its lowest level since November 3, 1993 on Thursday afternoon, after light fund selling took the market lower in New York, dealers said.
Bullion closed at $366.85 after fixing at $366.55 per ounce during the afternoon.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5407 marks and 115.47 yen compared with 1.5385 marks and 115.85 yen late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 61.1 points lower at 4,057.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 58.76 at 2,256.97.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 39.92 at 2,848.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $366.85 compared with its late level of $369.05 in London on Tuesday.
